speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of your rash and tell me if the numbness and tingling have worsened recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Is your occupation involving direct contact with pesticides or specific plants, and do you notice any scaling or blistering on the skin where the rash is most prominent? Additionally, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or muscle weakness in addition to the numbness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on upper body and face. I also have Numbness and tingling sensation of both palms, Thinning of the eyebrows, Loss of some eyelashes, Hypopigmented macules around the elbows.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Paraneoplastic Acrokeratoderma Blaine (associated with Scleroderma or Paraneoplastic Syndrome). Given the combination of pruritic rash, acral paresthesias, and alopecia hypotrichosis (eyebrow/eyelash loss), this constellation is highly suggestive of a paraneoplastic syndrome, often linked to underlying malignancy such as thymoma or lung cancer. I recommend immediate imaging to rule out an occult tumor.
